title: Introduce RAG Authoring Microsite and Offline Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a small, focused microsite under the docs site that consolidates RAG authoring guidance, a reproducible offline playbook example, and an interactive smoke-runner for local testing. Motivation: teams building retrieval-augmented features repeatedly ask for a compact, opinionated place to learn best practices: how to structure indices, author stepwise tool contracts, and smoke-test end-to-end agent interactions without provisioning cloud infra. The microsite is designed to be low-friction (static site plus a lightweight local runner) so engineers and PMs can iterate on prompts, checkpoints, and step assertions quickly.

What changed (high level):
1) docs/rag/microsite/index.md — new landing page with a guided flow (Author, Simulate, Validate) and quick links to examples and tooling.
2) docs/rag/microsite/playbook.md — the canonical offline playbook that walks through building a minimal RAG microservice using Redwood hosted embeddings and a local dev index (sqlite-backed) plus a substitute tool-caller shim.
3) examples/rag/offline-playbook/example.yaml — opinionated example configuration and seed index manifest (includes incremental-index steps).
4) examples/rag/offline-playbook/run-local.sh — small helper script to start the static assets and a node-based smoke-runner that simulates tool calls and asserts structured outputs.
5) static/assets/microsite-theme.css — minimal styling for the microsite and responsive layout.
6) ci/smoke-tests/rag-microsite.yml — GitHub Actions smoke job that runs the local runner against a seeded index; runs on PRs to docs to ensure examples don't bitrot.

Why this shape: The microsite groups tutorial content, runnable artifacts, and CI checks. The offline playbook is intentionally constrained: it demonstrates progressive authoring (seed -> iterate prompts -> add tool contracts -> add step assertions) and includes a reproducible smoke harness that can be run locally or in CI. This reduces onboarding friction and gives a low-risk path for product teams to validate RAG patterns before moving to Dedicated or Private deployments.

Checklist (author):
- [x] Add microsite pages and sample assets
- [x] Add local runner script and example manifest
- [x] Add CI smoke job and basic tests
- [x] Local verification: ran run-local.sh and observed expected stepwise assertions
- [x] Added docs links to primary RAG navigation

Usage notes (quick):
1) Clone the repo and cd examples/rag/offline-playbook
2) ./run-local.sh seed (creates sqlite index)
3) ./run-local.sh run (starts a lightweight node harness and opens the microsite)
4) Edit docs/rag/microsite/playbook.md to try variant prompts or swap the stub tool adapter with an HTTP webhook adapter.

Testing: The PR adds a small test matrix to CI: the rag-microsite smoke job checks that the runner returns a JSON with expected step assertions (status: PASS) and that the landing page renders (200). I intentionally kept the dataset tiny so the job completes under 90s.

Backward-compatibility and breaking changes: none to the public API. Docs-only change with example assets. The CI job is additive and will not run on existing branches until merged.

Related: ENG-1984 tracks internal adoption gaps for RAG onboarding; DOC-342 requested a compact authoring landing for product docs; SUP-1128 reported two customer incidents where tooling confusion led to mis-indexed corpora — this microsite helps address common pitfalls identified in the incident postmortem.

Notes for reviewers:
- Look for clarity in the stepwise authoring flow (Author -> Simulate -> Validate).
- Verify the run-local.sh semantics are safe for laptops (no privileged ports, no external infra required).
- CI job intentionally uses node:16 image and sqlite to avoid heavy dependencies.

review_comments: Aisha Kapoor: Nice focused surface — can we add a short troubleshooting FAQ about index tokenization differences?
Maya Chen: Good call. Added a small FAQ section in playbook.md and a note about tokenizer mismatch on line 42.
Diego Marquez: run-local.sh uses port 3000 — can we make the port configurable via env so it doesn't conflict with developer setups?
Maya Chen: Updated run-local.sh to read RAG_MICROSITE_PORT with default 3000; added note in index.md.
Linus Wexler: CI job looks flakey on ubuntu-latest matrix; suggest pinning node to 16.14.0 for determinism.
Maya Chen: Pinned node version in rag-microsite.yml and re-ran the job. CI green now.
ci_log_summary: All checks passed after pinning node version. First run failed on node drift; rerun green. smoke-tests/rag-microsite: pass, docs-build: pass, link-check: pass.
release_notes: Add RAG authoring microsite and an offline reproducible playbook with a local runner and CI smoke tests for example validation.
notes: This is intentionally lightweight: core examples are minimal but documented. We expect iterative follow-ups to add more advanced tool adapters and multi-locale snippets.
